subject: Sliding versus hinged wardrobe doors
hook: Sliding doors that drift open on their own nearly always have the same cause: a track that is not level.
ig:
Sliding doors that drift open on their own nearly always have the same cause: a track that is not level.

Gravity does the rest. A track that falls slightly to one side means the door creeps towards the low end, and you are forever nudging it back.

This is how we set sliding wardrobe doors up when we fit them:
• Check the head and floor for level before any track goes on
• Fix the top track and re-check it along its full length
• Line the bottom track up directly beneath it
• Hang the doors and adjust each one for height
• Check the gap down every edge, so doors meet evenly top to bottom

In older Staffordshire houses, floors and ceilings are rarely true, which is why this part never gets rushed.

Thinking about sliding wardrobe doors? DM us a photo of the wall and we will tell you what to look out for.
fb:
Got sliding wardrobe doors that will not stay put? There is a good chance the track is not quite level.

When our team fits sliding doors, the first job is checking the floor and ceiling, because in a lot of older homes neither is straight. The top track goes on and gets checked along its length, the bottom track is lined up beneath it, then each door is hung and adjusted until the gaps are even from top to bottom.

It is a few extra minutes that make the difference between doors that glide and doors that wander. See our fitted wardrobes here:
